title: Tail-supported Hardy control from the R-419 Lyapunov transform
question: Does the positive R-419 tail Lyapunov rate give an exact ground-state-transform identity and a Hardy-type Dirichlet lower bound for functions supported on the tail?
method: Keep the hash-pinned R-419 Q3 functional, log-domain conditional weights, momentum conductance and normalization unchanged on six selected volume/cutoff systems, three beta values and both collar orientations.
For each selected conditional row define V_i=exp(alpha*(max(log(pi))-log(pi_i))) with alpha=1/40 and tail threshold theta=4, then compute h_i=-(L V)_i/V_i.
Evaluate the exact reversible identity E(f)=sum_i pi_i h_i f_i^2 + 1/2 sum_ij c_ij V_i V_j(f_i/V_i-f_j/V_j)^2 on four deterministic vectors supported on the tail.
Use the nonnegative remainder and the minimum tail rate to check E(f)>=kappa sum_tail pi_i f_i^2, then rebuild the algebra independently on three non-importing reversible graph fixtures.
Run hostile sign, symmetry, positivity, support, omitted-remainder and forged-rate mutations, and compile the two-state algebraic Lean cross-check.
finding: The primary lane passes 6544/6544 assertions over 6 Q3 systems, 858 conditional rows and 1128 tail-supported test vectors; the independent non-importing lane passes 63/63 over 3 fixtures and 12 vectors; the hostile lane rejects 7/7 invalid mutations; the integrated verifier passes 19/19; and Lean R421 compiles. The primary minimum tail rate is 0.4188403678721089, maximum identity residual is 1.4210854715202004e-14, minimum ground-state remainder is 0.004172932635476484 and minimum Hardy slack is 0.004172932635476481. The independent maximum residual is 2.220446049250313e-16 and its minimum Hardy slack is 0.01951825515843849.
decision_reason: The reversible ground-state transform is an exact finite algebraic interface below the R-419 corridor. Its weighted-square remainder turns a positive tail drift into a tail-supported Dirichlet lower bound, which is a concrete input for a future variance decomposition. The result does not control arbitrary observables with a core component and supplies no uniform limit.

adversarial_review.check: Reversing h changes the tail lower-bound direction and is rejected.
Omitting the weighted square fails the two-state identity.
An asymmetric conductance matrix is rejected before applying the identity.
Nonpositive stationary weights or Lyapunov entries are rejected rather than regularized.
A vector nonzero on the core is rejected for the tail-only Hardy consequence.
A forged kappa above the actual tail minimum is rejected.
Finite tail-supported control is not promoted to global Poincare, common-core, GNS, continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap closure.

decision_scope: Finite exact identity and selected R-419 calibration; no tier change.
next_action: Prove a domain-controlled version on an unbounded Q3 Hamiltonian common core, then derive the missing core-mean and boundary-capacity variance decomposition and transfer it to the R-399/R-415 history before any global Poincare or GNS promotion.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite ground-state-transform and tail-supported Hardy interface. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform constant, no arbitrary-observable Poincare inequality, no common core, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The exact nonnegative remainder is a finite algebraic route advance; it is not evidence for physical tail control, a uniform coercive estimate, a Yang-Mills result or a mass gap.
